title: Frontend Observability
description: Web Vitals, errors and API timings as the browser experiences them. Collected by ui/src/observability, ingested at POST /api/telemetry, exposed on the API /metrics endpoint Prometheus already scrapes, and logged through the Alloy pipeline that already ships backend logs. Product analytics is deliberately absent: PostHog owns that.

panels.title: Page views
panels.description: Route activations in the selected period. A total rather than a rate: at this volume a per-second rate over a short window is empty, and an empty panel reads as broken when the answer is a number. PostHog owns product analytics; this is here so the other panels can be read against traffic.

panels.title: Errors
panels.description: Every kind of frontend error in the period, including ones no user noticed.

panels.title: API failure rate
panels.description: Share of browser-observed calls that returned 4xx, 5xx, or never answered at all.

panels.title: LCP p75
panels.description: Largest Contentful Paint. Good <= 2.5s, poor > 4s.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.75, sum by (le) (rate(frontend_web_vitals_seconds_bucket{metric="LCP", environment=~"$environment", route=~"$route", device=~"$device"}[$__range])))

panels.title: INP p75
panels.description: Interaction to Next Paint. Good <= 200ms, poor > 500ms.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.75, sum by (le) (rate(frontend_web_vitals_seconds_bucket{metric="INP", environment=~"$environment", route=~"$route", device=~"$device"}[$__range])))

panels.title: CLS p75
panels.description: Cumulative Layout Shift, unitless. Good <= 0.1, poor > 0.25.

panels.title: TTFB p95
panels.description: Time to first byte as the browser measured it.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(frontend_web_vitals_seconds_bucket{metric="TTFB", environment=~"$environment", route=~"$route", device=~"$device"}[$__range])))

panels.title: API p95
panels.description: Browser-side latency: includes DNS, TLS and network the backend histogram never sees.

panels.title: Reporting builds
panels.description: How many distinct frontend builds are currently reporting. More than one during a rollout is normal; for hours afterwards means stale tabs.

panels.title: Events dropped
panels.description: Rejected by the ingest endpoint. A steady non-zero rate means a client is sending something the schema does not accept.

panels.title: Deployed build
panels.description: The build browsers are currently reporting. Shows the label, not the gauge value - the value is always 1 by construction, which is what this panel displayed before.

panels.title: LCP percentiles
panels.description: p50, p75 and p95 of LCP. p75 is the number Google reports on; p50 is the typical user and p95 the tail that complains.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le) (rate(frontend_web_vitals_seconds_bucket{metric="LCP", environment=~"$environment", route=~"$route", device=~"$device"}[$__rate_interval])))
histogram_quantile(0.75, sum by (le) (rate(frontend_web_vitals_seconds_bucket{metric="LCP", environment=~"$environment", route=~"$route", device=~"$device"}[$__rate_interval])))
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(frontend_web_vitals_seconds_bucket{metric="LCP", environment=~"$environment", route=~"$route", device=~"$device"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: CLS percentiles
panels.description: Layout shift is a unitless score, so it lives in its own metric instead of being averaged in with durations.

panels.title: LCP p75 by route (worst 10)
panels.description: Which screens are slow, rather than whether the app is slow.

targets.expr: topk(10, histogram_quantile(0.75, sum by (le, route) (rate(frontend_web_vitals_seconds_bucket{metric="LCP", environment=~"$environment", route=~"$route", device=~"$device"}[$__rate_interval]))))

panels.title: LCP p75 by device
panels.description: Mobile and desktop rarely regress together. One moving alone usually means layout or asset weight.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.75, sum by (le, device) (rate(frontend_web_vitals_seconds_bucket{metric="LCP", environment=~"$environment", route=~"$route", device=~"$device"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: INP p75 by device
panels.description: Interaction latency is where a slow device shows up first.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.75, sum by (le, device) (rate(frontend_web_vitals_seconds_bucket{metric="INP", environment=~"$environment", route=~"$route", device=~"$device"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Vitals sample volume
panels.description: What the percentiles above rest on. A p95 over three samples is noise, and this panel is how you notice.

panels.title: API calls, as the browser sees them
Latency percentiles
panels.description: Browser-side timing. A gap between this and the backend histogram is network, queueing or the client itself.

panels.title: Slowest endpoints (p95)
panels.description: Endpoints are normalised, so /api/users/1 and /api/users/2 are one line rather than two thousand.

panels.title: Calls per minute by endpoint
panels.description: Volume, for reading the latency panels honestly and for spotting a render loop hammering one endpoint.

panels.title: Outcome mix
panels.description: status_class rather than the exact code, to keep the series count flat. "unknown" means no response ever arrived: CORS, DNS, a dropped connection or a timeout.

panels.title: Errors per minute by kind
panels.description: chunk_load spiking right after a deploy is the signature of an open tab whose hashed assets no longer exist. The fix is a reload prompt, not a code change.

panels.title: Errors per minute by route (top 10)
panels.description: Where they happen.

panels.title: Errors by browser
panels.description: A fault in one engine only is usually a polyfill or an unsupported API.

panels.title: Errors by device
panels.description: Splits a viewport-specific fault from a general one.

panels.title: Top error fingerprints
panels.description: Grouped by the shape of the error rather than its message, so one fault is one line even when the message embeds a changing id.

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (error_name, fingerprint) (count_over_time({job="server"} | json | component="frontend" | error_kind != "third_party_resource" | client_environment =~ "$environment" | error_name != "" [$__interval])))

panels.title: Frontend events in Loki
panels.description: Written by the API as it ingests each browser event, so they travel the same Alloy pipeline as every other backend log. request_id here is the same id the backend recorded for that call: paste it into the Performance Tracker Logs dashboard to see the server side of the same request.
